From 4177f545895b1da08447a80692f30617154efa6e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2022 10:17:48 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] tcp: Fix data-races around sysctl_tcp_migrate_req.

While reading sysctl_tcp_migrate_req, it can be changed concurrently.
Thus, we need to add READ_ONCE() to its readers.

Fixes: f9ac779f881c ("net: Introduce net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req.")
Signed-off-by: Kuniyuki Iwashima <kuniyu@amazon.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/core/sock_reuseport.c b/net/core/sock_reuseport.c
index 3f00a28fe762..5daa1fa54249 100644
--- a/net/core/sock_reuseport.c
+++ b/net/core/sock_reuseport.c
@@ -387,7 +387,7 @@ void reuseport_stop_listen_sock(struct sock *sk)
 		prog = rcu_dereference_protected(reuse->prog,
 						 lockdep_is_held(&reuseport_lock));
 
-		if (sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req ||
+		if (READ_ONCE(sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req) ||
 		    (prog && prog->expected_attach_type == BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE)) {
 			/* Migration capable, move sk from the listening section
 			 * to the closed section.
@@ -545,7 +545,7 @@ struct sock *reuseport_migrate_sock(struct sock *sk,
 	hash = migrating_sk->sk_hash;
 	prog = rcu_dereference(reuse->prog);
 	if (!prog || prog->expected_attach_type != BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE) {
-		if (sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req)
+		if (READ_ONCE(sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req))
 			goto select_by_hash;
 		goto failure;
 	}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/core/sock_reuseport.c`**
   - **Line 387**: The condition checking `sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req` was modified to use `READ_ONCE()`, ensuring that the value is read atomically to prevent data races.
   - **Line 545**: Similarly, the condition checking `sock_net(sk)->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_migrate_req` was also modified to use `READ_ONCE()` for the same reason.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `net/core/sock_reuseport.c` are related in that they both address the same issue of potential data races when accessing the `sysctl_tcp_migrate_req` variable. By using `READ_ONCE()`, the patch ensures that the value read from `sysctl_tcp_migrate_req` is consistent and not subject to concurrent modifications, thereby enhancing the thread safety of the code. Both changes are part of a broader effort to fix the data race issue identified in the bug report associated with the patch.
